description:
Connect your devices into a secure WireGuard®-based overlay network with SSO, MFA and granular access controls.

NetBird combines a configuration-free peer-to-peer private network and a centralized access control system in a single platform, making it easy to create secure private networks for your organization or home.
Connect. NetBird creates a WireGuard-based overlay network that automatically connects your machines over an encrypted tunnel, leaving behind the hassle of opening ports, complex firewall rules, VPN gateways, and so forth.
Secure. NetBird enables secure remote access by applying granular access policies while allowing you to manage them intuitively from a single place. Works universally on any infrastructure.
Release Notes for v0.82.0
Highlights
🛣️ Latency-aware HA routing that holds stable routes
Routing peers in an HA group with equal metrics are meant to be chosen by latency, but the client used to sample latency only once, when the connection was set up, and moved the route on events that did not need it. Every switch between masquerading routing peers resets the TCP connections using the route, so SSH sessions and other long-lived flows dropped more often than they had to.
The client now samples the latency of connected routing peers continuously and smooths it, and moves a route for latency only when the gain clears a margin: at least 20ms, 20% of the current latency, and the measurement noise of both paths. After a latency-driven switch it keeps the new peer for at least 30 seconds. A routing peer that drops from direct to relay keeps the route for a grace period before it moves to an equivalent direct peer, and a peer that comes up over relay first is held the same way while the others turn direct. Failover, better metrics and connected-over-idle still switch immediately.
The grace period is set on the client with NB_HA_RELAYED_SWITCH_DELAY (a duration, 0, or never; default 30s). Routing peer switches are now logged at warning level with the reason and published as system events, so they show in netbird status -d and in debug bundles.
📖 High availability for routing peers · #7689, #8192
📋 netbird status --table
netbird status --table (-t) lists peers in a table with their name, IP, status, connection type, latency and traffic, which is easier to scan than the detailed output on a large network. It works with the existing filter flags, so netbird status -t -S connected -T P2P shows only connected peer-to-peer peers.
Peers (3/5 connected):
NAME          IP            STATUS       CONN      LATENCY   RX / TX
web-01        100.64.0.12   Connected    P2P       12ms      1.2 MiB / 3.4 MiB
db-01         100.64.0.15   Connected    Relayed   48ms      54.0 KiB / 12.1 KiB
ci-runner     100.64.0.40   Connecting   -         -         0 B / 0 B
--table cannot be combined with -d, --json, --yaml, --ipv4 or --ipv6.
📖 CLI: status, table view · #8305
🗄️ A dedicated database for reverse proxy access logs
Reverse proxy access logs are now read and written through their own database connection instead of the main store's, and can live in a separate database. Nothing needs to change on upgrade: by default the access log store follows the main store engine, as a separate access_logs.db file in the data directory on SQLite, or the main store DSN through its own connection pool on PostgreSQL.
To point it elsewhere, set server.accessLogStore (engine, dsn, file) in the combined server's config.yaml, or the environment variables below:

| Variable                         | Purpose                                          |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| NB_ACCESS_LOG_STORE_ENGINE       | sqlite or postgres                               |
| NB_ACCESS_LOG_POSTGRES_DSN       | a dedicated PostgreSQL database                  |
| NB_ACCESS_LOG_SQLITE_FILE        | the SQLite file, access_logs.db by default       |
| NB_ACCESS_LOG_SQL_MAX_OPEN_CONNS | pool size, falling back to NB_SQL_MAX_OPEN_CONNS |

📖 Reverse proxy access logs · #8303
Removal: MySQL store
The MySQL store engine for management, deprecated in v0.81.0, is removed. A management server configured with the mysql engine refuses to start on v0.82.0 and points to the migration guide.
Migrate to PostgreSQL before upgrading. The netbird-mysql-migrate tool is no longer part of the release, so run the migration while still on 0.81.x, with the tool from the v0.81.5 release, then upgrade.
📖 Migrate from MySQL to PostgreSQL · #7914
Deprecation: Rosenpass
Rosenpass support is deprecated. It keeps working for now, but it may be removed in a future release, so avoid making new deployments depend on it. --enable-rosenpass and --rosenpass-permissive are hidden from netbird up --help and print a deprecation warning whenever they are used, and the desktop app shows a notice under the quantum-resistance toggle in Settings → Security.
📖 Post-quantum cryptography (Rosenpass) · #8372
What's New
🔒 Security and Access Control
- Applied the SSH root-login setting to every uid 0 account, not only to the account named root, so aliases such as FreeBSD's toor are covered; an account whose uid cannot be parsed is treated as privileged. #8390
- Refused path-bearing LANGUAGE/LC_*, TERM and TZ values from SSH clients before they reach the privileged login/su call for a session. #8388
- Matched the account id from the request against the service configuration in the reverse proxy's auth and access log middleware. #8386
- Masked credentials in URLs written to the management logs. #8250
🖥️ Client Improvements
- Detected default route changes in the Linux network monitor. #8216
- Kept the resolv.conf watch armed while repairing DNS in file mode. #8207
- Fixed a deadlock when shutting down the Signal reconnect listener. #8257
- Called the disconnect callback on every connection teardown. #8178
- Skipped peers without a PTR record in the Kubernetes commands. #8360
- Stopped the service and the UI before the Windows installer extracts files. #8255
- Moved the macOS Homebrew cask to Homebrew install steps. #7477
- Migrated the desktop UI to Tailwind CSS 4 and fixed the frontend npm audit findings, and bumped the wails fork to v3.0.0. #8277, #8370
- Added Hebrew to the language picker, and fixed the grammar of the post-install message. #8102, #8242
- Removed the non-functional --admin-url flag; it is now deprecated and ignored. #8267
- Bumped wireguard-go and removed the replace directives from the embedded client module. #8229, #8280
⚙️ Management Improvements
- Moved network map data reads onto a PostgreSQL read replica when NB_STORE_ENGINE_POSTGRES_REPLICA_DSN is set; without it, reads stay on the primary. #8302
- Sped up common queries with new indexes for groups, events, personal access tokens and access logs, an index-friendly inner groups query, a faster posture check cache and fewer last-usage writes for users and tokens. #8289, #8297, #8366, #8290
- Pushed network maps when an integrated validator changes a peer's approval outside a login, for example during a periodic EDR sync, so a newly approved peer no longer waits for an unrelated update. #8299
- Gave the /api/setup owner account the single account mode domain, so the first JIT user joins it instead of getting an account of their own. #8147
- Used the account owner as the inviter for service user invites. #8276
- Added pagination to the GetAllPeers call. #8190
- Skipped the inactivity expiration rescan on connect when a job is already scheduled, and cancelled peer expiration for accounts that no longer exist. #8287, #8218
- Handled a possible nil peer when returning an empty network map, and cleaned NUL bytes from peer metadata strings. #8285, #8219
🔀 Reverse Proxy
- Added --external-ip-map to the proxy's embedded client (NB_PROXY_EXTERNAL_IP_MAP), so a proxy in a container or behind NAT can advertise its public address and peers reach it directly instead of over relay. It needs a fixed, forwarded --wg-port, so it applies to single-account deployments. #8185
- Returned the reason when custom domain validation fails. #8122
- Fixed the proxy connection lifecycle during acknowledgements. #8220
📡 Signal and Relay
- The relay server now negotiates the protocol version instead of rejecting clients that send a different one, and skips unknown message types after authentication. Current clients still get v1 and the same bytes as before; this lets later client versions change the protocol without upgrading every relay first. The handshake size limit grows from 212 to 8192 bytes. #8231
🏗️ Infrastructure and CI
- Restricted the FreeBSD port job to stable releases. #8204
- Raised the WASM build size limit to 70MB. #8281
- Announced tag-pushed releases on the forum. #8265
- Let test suites outside the module reach the e2e harness network, and fixed errcheck findings from the latest golangci-lint. #8260, #8251
📝 Misc
- New translations from Crowdin. #8101
Dashboard (v2.96.0)
- Saved target edits made from the network and peer pages. dashboard#863
- Refined the RDP certificate prompt. dashboard#874
- Fixed crashes: browser translation no longer breaks the dashboard, and resetting a table page while server data loads no longer crashes. dashboard#867, dashboard#868
- Updated Next.js to 16.4.3 and Tailwind CSS to v4, fixed the npm audit findings and the white outline flash on button click that came with Tailwind v4. dashboard#852, dashboard#876, dashboard#866
- Updated the announcements with the v0.81 features and bumped the embedded WASM client to v0.81.5. dashboard#861, dashboard#859, dashboard#862, dashboard#875
- Fixed flaky Control Center draft end-to-end tests. dashboard#869, dashboard#864
